repaired.name: Scenario
repaired.script:
triggered := false
if (triggered == true) {
wait until(not (all(#PresenceSensor).presenceSensor_presence == true))
triggered = false
}
wait until(all(#PresenceSensor).presenceSensor_presence == true)
all(#ColorControl).colorControl_setColor("purple")
triggered = true

diagnosis.summary: The IR requires a rising-edge wait for PresenceSensor.Presence == true before calling ColorControl.SetColor. The candidate uses a periodic `if` which only evaluates at the start of the 1000 ms cycle. At t=100 ms, the sensor became true, but the candidate's `if` had already passed, so it missed the event. The fix implements the rising-edge pattern: block until the condition becomes true (after clearing the 'fired' state), then execute the body.
diagnosis.change_summary: Replaced the periodic `if` guard with a blocking two-wait rearm pattern (`wait until(not C)` then `wait until(C)`). This ensures the action fires exactly when the sensor transitions to true, matching the IR's rising-edge requirement, rather than only at the start of each 1-second period.
